source.title: Open Problems for the Bath-Beijing-Paris Branching Structures Meeting, 14th-18th May 2018

accepted.question_text: For one-dimensional branching random walk, can the fine near-critical and critical results known for branching Brownian motion with negative drift and killing at the origin be extended to the random-walk setting, including precise survival and scaling results analogous to the branching-Brownian-motion results near the critical drift? In particular, can one develop the more refined estimates needed for random walks conditioned to stay in an interval [a, b] or between two curves, beyond first-order Mogul'skii-type asymptotics?
accepted.context_brief: Near-critical branching random walk

evidence.quote: Adapting these and other results to branching random walk seems like a tough and inter- esting problem. The major hurdle seems to be to obtain precise estimates on random walks conditioned to stay in an interval [a, b] or, more generally, between two curves.

A typical result in this direction is Mogul’skii’s estimate [13], which gives the first order in the (expo- nential) decay of such a probability. It seems that more refined estimates are needed and no general theory seems to be available up to now.

accepted.question_text: In branching Brownian motion whose infinitesimal variance at time t in [0, T] is sigma(t/T)^2 for a prescribed function sigma:[0,1]->R_+, if m_T = vT - wT^(1/3) - sigma(1) log T is the centering for the maximum M_T in the strictly decreasing smooth case, can one prove convergence in distribution of M_T - m_T rather than only tightness?
accepted.context_brief: Time-inhomogeneous BBM maximum

evidence.quote: This model has been well studied, but fine limit theorems are still lacking.
We have shown that there exists explicit constants v and w, such that the family of random variables (MT − mT )T ≥0 is tight... An obvious next step is to prove convergence in distribution.

accepted.question_text: For the same time-inhomogeneous branching Brownian motion model, can one prove convergence of the extremal point process and describe the genealogy of the maximal particles, for example by showing convergence of a suitable statistic to Neveu's continuous-state branching process?
accepted.context_brief: Extremal process and genealogy in BBM

evidence.quote: I believe that this can be handled as in BBM with absorption [3, 6], namely by showing convergence of a suitable statistic to Neveu’s CSBP. This approach would then also allow to show convergence of the extremal process. It would also provide a way of studying the genealogy of the maximal particles.

accepted.question_text: For branching Brownian motion with time-varying variance, what is the large-deviation behavior of the maximum: what is the probability that the maximum is a constant factor larger than its typical value, and what does the process look like when conditioned on that event?
accepted.context_brief: Large deviations of BBM maximum

evidence.quote: Another interesting question is large deviation behavior of the maximum, i.e., what is the probability that the maximum is a constant times larger than its typical value and what does the process look like conditioned on this event?

accepted.question_text: For N-branching random walk with selection of the N right-most particles at every step, what happens for displacement distributions in the intermediate regime between light-tailed laws with an exponential moment and the regularly varying polynomial-tail laws already analyzed? In particular, can one determine the speed and qualitative behavior in these subexponential but not regularly varying regimes?
accepted.context_brief: N-branching random walk with heavy tails

evidence.quote: A natural question and possibility for future research is to investigate what happens in between the two scenarios of light-tailed displacement distributions (satisfying an exponential moment assumption) and the polynomial tails considered in the present article.
This seems to be a delicate and interesting question. Even the heuristic picture is not clear.

accepted.question_text: For N-branching random walk with subexponential displacement distributions, is the advance of the particle cloud always caused by jumps of single particles, as in the regularly varying case, or can particle interaction create genuinely different leading mechanisms?
accepted.context_brief: Mechanism of advance under subexponential tails

evidence.quote: For example, it is not clear to us whether for all subexponential displacement distributions the advance of the cloud of particles arises from jumps of single particles as is the case for the regularly varying tails considered here.

accepted.question_text: For N-branching random walk with subexponential displacement distributions, is the genealogy always described by the star-shaped coalescent, meaning the coalescent in which all particles merge into a single block at once, as conjectured in the regularly varying case?
accepted.context_brief: Genealogy of N-branching random walk

evidence.quote: In the regularly varying case, we believe (but have not shown) the genealogy to be described by the star-shaped coalescent (i.e. the coalescent where all particles coagulate to a single block). Does this coalescent describe the genealogy of N -BRW for every subexponential displacement distribution?

accepted.question_text: For 0 < alpha < 1, can one construct a two-parameter analogue of the Fleming-Viot process whose reversible measure, or at least stationary distribution, is the two-parameter Dirichlet process Dirichlet(theta, alpha, nu_0)?
accepted.context_brief: Two-parameter Fleming-Viot process

evidence.quote: Open Problem: Can one generalize the Fleming-Viot process to the two-parameter setting with 0 < α < 1 so that Dirichlet(θ, α, ν0 ) is its reversible measure or stationary distribution?

accepted.question_text: For a continuous multiplicative graph whose law is characterized by an increasing function psi:(0, infinity)->(0, infinity), is the sufficient compactness condition integral from 1 to infinity of d lambda / psi(lambda) being finite actually sharp?
accepted.context_brief: Compactness criterion for continuous multiplicative graphs

evidence.quote: Problem 1. The law of a continuous multiplicative graph is characterised by an increasing function ψ : (0, ∞) → (0, ∞). We have proved that if 1 dλ/ψ(λ) < ∞, then the limiting graph is compact. Question: Is this condition sharp ?

accepted.question_text: Let B^b and B^r be independent one-dimensional Brownian motions started from 0, define time changes theta^b_t, Lambda^b_t, Lambda^r_t as in the source, and then define B_t = B^b(Lambda^b_t) + B^r(Lambda^r_t). Since B is again a one-dimensional Brownian motion started from 0, is it possible to recover B^b and B^r from B in a measurable way?
accepted.context_brief: Measurable Brownian decomposition

evidence.quote: It turns out that B is a one-dimensional Brownian motion with initial value 0. Question: Is it possible to derive B b and B r from B in a measurable way ?

accepted.question_text: Can one establish spatial limit theorems for superprocesses and branching Markov processes, such as laws of large numbers, L log L criteria, and central limit theorems, without assuming that the mean semigroup has discrete spectrum, thereby including cases such as super-Brownian motion?
accepted.context_brief: Spatial limit theorems without discrete spectrum

evidence.quote: This excludes the case of super Brownian motions. It is natural to ask for versions of these spatial limit theorems without this discrete spectrum assumption.

accepted.question_text: For CLE_kappa nesting fields with kappa in (8/3, 8), when the field is built from a nested CLE_kappa and i.i.d. loop weights with law mu, are the loops used to build the nesting field determined by the field itself for values of kappa other than 4 and for more general laws mu, as happens in the Gaussian free field case kappa = 4?
accepted.context_brief: Loop reconstruction from CLE nesting field

evidence.quote: When the Gaussian free field is constructed as a nesting field with κ = 4, it is known that the loops used to build it are deterministic given the field. Is this true for other values of κ and laws µ?

accepted.question_text: What can be said about the extremal process of the CLE_kappa nesting field?
accepted.context_brief: Extremal process of CLE nesting field

evidence.quote: What can one say about the extremal process of the CLEκ nesting field?

accepted.question_text: In branching Brownian motion, if mu_t denotes the median position of the rightmost particle and satisfies Bramson's front-location asymptotic, can one prove the asymptotic expansion for the instantaneous velocity of the front, namely partial_t mu_t = 2 - 3/(2t) + o(t^(-1)) as t tends to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Velocity asymptotics for BBM front

evidence.quote: There seems to be no result for an asymptotic expansion for the instan- taneous velocity ∂t µt of the front. However (ask any physicist), it is certain that ∂ t µt = 2 − 3/(2t) + o(t−1 ), as t → ∞. Can one prove it ?

accepted.question_text: Can the same front-velocity asymptotic partial_t mu_t = 2 - 3/(2t) + o(t^(-1)) be proved for other natural definitions of the front position in branching Brownian motion, including the expected position of the rightmost particle and its most likely position?
accepted.context_brief: Velocity asymptotics for alternative front positions

evidence.quote: There are various ways one could define the position of the front µt and still have the expansion (1) hold... Then can one prove that (3) also hold for these positions?

accepted.question_text: If the initial condition for the F-KPP front decays sufficiently fast so that Bramson's front-location expansion still holds, can one also prove the same instantaneous-velocity asymptotic partial_t mu_t = 2 - 3/(2t) + o(t^(-1)) for those more general initial conditions?
accepted.context_brief: Velocity asymptotics under other initial data

evidence.quote: What about different initial conditions ? If h(x, 0) decays fast enough, then (1) still holds (with a different value for a...) So should (3), but can one prove it ?

accepted.question_text: For branching Brownian motion front positions, can one prove higher-derivative asymptotics partial_t^n mu_t = (-1)^n 3(n-1)!/(2 t^n) + o(t^(-n)) for every integer n at least 2?
accepted.context_brief: Higher derivatives of BBM front position

evidence.quote: Why stop at the first derivative ? Do we have ∂tn µt = (−1)n 3(n − 1)!/(2tn) + o(t−n ), t → ∞, n ≥ 2?

accepted.question_text: Can one rigorously justify differentiating the refined Bramson expansion for the branching Brownian motion front in order to obtain the sharper velocity expansion that includes the t^(-3/2) correction and the t^(-2) log t term?
accepted.context_brief: Sharper BBM velocity expansion

evidence.quote: Bramson’s expansion can be refined... Then one should have ... but a proof might be needed.

accepted.question_text: In branching Brownian motion with decay of mass, for each m in (0,1), can one at least prove the weaker statement that there exist exponents a and b with 0 < a < 1/3 < b < 1 such that, almost surely, the left front gap sqrt(2)t - d(t,m) grows faster than t^a while the right front gap sqrt(2)t - D(t,m) is little-o of t^b?
accepted.context_brief: Weaker front-gap bounds with decay of mass

evidence.quote: Even showing that there exist 0 < a < 13 < b < 1 such that almost surely ... would be a new result.

accepted.question_text: In branching Brownian motion with decay of mass, can the current upper bound on the largest particle mass be improved substantially, given the belief that the largest particle mass decays much more quickly than the existing polynomial-style bound?
accepted.context_brief: Largest particle mass with decay of mass

evidence.quote: Question 2: In [?], we proved the following upper bound on the largest particle mass... We believe that in fact the largest particle mass decays much more quickly - can we improve on this upper bound?

accepted.question_text: Consider the individual-based Darwinian-evolution model on trait space X = R^d in which an individual of trait x has birth rate Kr(x)+b(x), natural death rate Kr(x)+d(x), mutation probability p(x) with mutation kernel m_K, and competition kernel c(x,y), and let nu denote the continuous measure-valued superprocess obtained as the K->infinity limit in Theorem 1. Does this limiting measure-valued process nu admit a density, at least in dimension d = 1 as one expects by analogy with super-Brownian motion?
accepted.context_brief: Density of the limiting superprocess

evidence.quote: we formally introduce our interacting particle Markov process for Darwinian evolution in an asexual population with non-constant population size in which each individual is characterized by hereditary types.
Problem 1. Is there a density for the limiting measure-valued process ν in Theorem 1? One could expect
a positive answer when d = 1, as for the Super-Brownian motion; see for example [8] and reference there for general background.

accepted.question_text: For the same individual-based model and its limiting measure-valued superprocess nu, what can be said about extinction versus survival probabilities, and about the distribution of extinction times, both for the global population and for different sub-populations?
accepted.context_brief: Extinction and survival in Darwinian particle systems

evidence.quote: Problem 2. What can we say about the extinction (or survival) probability and the distribution of the extinction time of the different sub-populations or the global population?.

accepted.question_text: For the same individual-based model and limiting measure-valued superprocess nu, what can be said about quasi-stationary distributions in the regime where extinction of the population occurs almost surely?
accepted.context_brief: Quasi-stationarity for limiting superprocesses

evidence.quote: Problem 3. What can we say about the quasi-stationary distributions (assuming that the population will be extinct almost surely) ?.

accepted.question_text: For the same Darwinian-evolution setting, can one describe the genealogies both in the microscopic individual-based particle system and in the macroscopic limiting measure-valued model?
accepted.context_brief: Genealogies in microscopic and macroscopic models

evidence.quote: Problem 4. Is it possible to provide a description of the genealogies in the proposed (microscopic) individual-based model in Section 2, and the limiting (macroscopic) model in Theorem 1?

trace.notes: Mapped the PDF into contributor sections on pages 2-18 and identified open-problem regions in the Maillard, Feng, Duquesne-Broutin-Wang, Song, Powell, Brunet, Penington, and Berzunza-Sturm-Winter contributions.
Extracted explicit problem statements and implicit open questions from the identified sections; retained 24 items that could be rewritten from the source text and set aside 7 items needing review.

Moved items to needs_review when the source relied on undefined external constructions, undefined source-specific terms, or an unresolved constant that could not be made fully self-contained from the visible PDF text alone.
